parser: src/readability.py parse_mesh_terms() -- DescriptorName + every nested Term String, lowercased, 1-character terms dropped
why_not_committed: 298.5 MB uncompressed and it is NLM's file to distribute, not ours. Pinned by hash instead, the same way data/medqa_base.manifest.json pins the MedQA source.
why_pinned: med_term_density in askdocs_metrics.csv, meqsum_metrics.csv and medqa_stems_metrics.csv was computed against a MeSH file that was never committed and never pinned, so those numbers could not be reproduced or even checked by anyone. This manifest closes that: re-download, verify the sha256, and the density column is reconstructible.
reproduce: curl -o desc2026.zip https://nlmpubs.nlm.nih.gov/projects/mesh/MESH_FILES/xmlmesh/desc2026.zip && unzip desc2026.zip && sha256sum desc2026.xml
caveat: The existing corpus density numbers predate this pin, so they are asserted to have used a 2026 descriptor file, not proven to. Anything computed from this manifest forward is verifiable; the earlier corpus columns are only verifiable if they were produced from a file with this same hash, which is untested.
